name: LG Energy Solution, Ltd. (LG에너지솔루션)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: LG Energy Solution is executing the sharpest EV-to-ESS pivot among the Korean cell makers — ESS revenue grew ~4.6x YoY in H1 2026 to the high-20% of revenue, anchored by North American manufacturing that Chinese rivals cannot match under FEOC rules — but profitability remains dependent on US production tax credits, with operating losses ex-credits in most recent quarters. BACKGROUND: Spun off from LG Chem in December 2020 (battery heritage to 1947), Seoul-based LGES is the world's #3 EV battery maker (9.2% share in 2025 per SNE Research). It makes pouch (NCMA, and new LFP/mid-nickel lines) and cylindrical (2170, 46-Series) cells, ESS cells-to-containers, and runs LG Energy Solution Vertech, a US turnkey BESS system integrator. Production sites in 6 countries; 100,000+ battery patents claimed.
ecosystemRole: We assess LGES as the ecosystem's premier non-Chinese ESS supply chain: five North American ESS production sites targeting ~50 GWh of NA cell output by end-2026 (global >60 GWh, >80% NA), a 140 GWh ESS order backlog (end-2025), and the Vertech integration arm delivering turnkey BESS. Its own strategy deck frames the growth market as AI data centers explicitly — BESS + UPS + BBU — claiming it is the only supplier serving all three AI-DC storage applications with a non-FEOC supply chain. H1 2026 ESS shipments grew +357% YoY (SNE), with ~86% going to North America.

productsAndServices.name: ESS Batteries & Systems (cells → containers)
productsAndServices.category: Energy storage · ~high-20% of H1 2026 revenue and rising
productsAndServices.description: Grid, C&I, UPS, and residential storage: pouch LFP cells (JF1 56.6 Ah; JF2 159.2 Ah — US production from Q1 2026; JF3 >500 Wh next), NCM JH4 cells, containerized DC systems (JF1 DC LINK 2.4 at 2.45 MWh; JH4 DC LINK 2.8 at 2.86 MWh), and RESU/enblock residential lines. Roadmap: North-America-made prismatic LFP prototypes, a next-gen LFP product with 15% total-cost reduction shipping from 2028 (already contracted), and sodium-ion ESS samples to customers in 2027.
highlights: ESS order backlog 140 GWh at end-2025; 2026 targets: >90 GWh of new ESS orders and >60 GWh of ESS cell capacity (>80% North American)
Tesla Megapack 3 LFP cell supplier — $4.3B deal, production from 2027 at Lansing, MI (confirmed via US government filings, March 2026); company cites 12% higher energy density and up to 15,000 cycles
H1 2026: >KRW 3T of new ESS contracts including AI-data-center deals; ESS revenue ~4.6x YoY
DTE Energy (Michigan): 6 GWh/1.5 GW across 8 projects — grid buildout serving the Oracle-managed OpenAI data center; PGE (Poland) 981 MWh from the Wrocław plant

The wedge is regulatory: FEOC/tariff rules push US buyers toward non-Chinese cells that only Korean suppliers make locally at scale.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess LGES is converting EV overcapacity into an ESS franchise faster than any peer: EV JV lines (Ultium Tennessee, Honda JV, NextStar) are being pointed at ESS cells, capex is cut >40% for 2026, and ESS went from single-digit to high-20% of revenue in a year. Basis: company disclosures and SNE shipment data (+357% YoY H1 2026).

(High confidence) We assess the durable advantage is regulatory, not technical: FEOC/tariff rules and domestic-content credits make LGES's five-site North American ESS network the default non-Chinese supply chain for US storage — the Tesla Megapack 3 contract and DTE/Qcells/Excelsior pipeline are direct evidence.

(Moderate confidence) We assess profitability quality is the central vulnerability: consensus misses in 3 of the last 4 reported quarters, and ex-AMPC operating losses in most quarters from Q4 2024 through Q2 2026 — the equity story currently rests on US production credits persisting and ESS margin maturing before credits taper.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the AI data-center thesis is explicit company strategy, not narrative garnish: the IR deck names AI-DC expansion (UPS/BBU scale-up, grid-bottleneck-driven BESS) as the demand driver and claims unique coverage of all three AI-DC storage applications — H1 2026's >KRW 3T of ESS contracts 'including AI DC' begins to corroborate it.
(Low confidence) The reported Google Steel River supply role (~2.9 GWh, per Seoul Economic Daily citing industry sources) is not company-confirmed — treat as unverified until disclosed.
